hook.line: In the café this week every customer has a rumour: it closes, it is sold, Tomás is leaving. Tomás needs a way to pass the news along without signing his name under it, and a way to say what he is not claiming.
hook.es: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.

examples.es: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.
Supuestamente, el café cierra en diciembre.
examples.en: Supposedly, the café closes in December.

examples.es: No es que dude de ti.
examples.en: It's not that I doubt you.

examples.es: Por lo visto, Altamira ya compró tres edificios.
examples.en: Apparently, Altamira has already bought three buildings.

examples.es: Al parecer, Tomás se vuelve a Canadá.
examples.en: Apparently, Tomás is going back to Canada.

examples.es: No es que Vale no quiera ayudar.
examples.en: It's not that Vale doesn't want to help.

examples.es: Por lo visto, nadie sabe dónde está.
examples.en: Apparently, nobody knows where it is.

rule:
Two ways to keep your distance from a claim.

*Al parecer*, *por lo visto* and *supuestamente* sit at the start of the sentence and mean "apparently" or "supposedly". You are passing the news on, not vouching for it. The verb stays plain: *era*, *cierra*, *compró*. *Supuestamente* adds a raised eyebrow: you doubt it a little.

*No es que* is for what you are not saying: "it's not that...". The verb takes the wish form, because you are pushing the idea away: *no es que dude*, *no es que no quiera*.

English does the first with an adverb too, but for the second it just changes your tone of voice.
smallPrint: Teachers call these attenuators and evidential adverbs, and *no es que* is followed by the subjunctive.

readAndPick.es: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.
options: I am sure the permit was fake.
Apparently, the permit was fake.
The permit will be fake.

readAndPick.es: Supuestamente, el café cierra en diciembre.
options: The café closed in December.
The café definitely closes in December.
Supposedly, the café closes in December.

readAndPick.es: No es que dude de ti.
options: It's not that I doubt you.
I doubt you.
You doubt me.

readAndPick.es: Por lo visto, nadie sabe dónde está.
options: I saw nobody there.
Nobody has seen where it is.
Apparently, nobody knows where it is.

readAndPick.es: No es que Vale no quiera ayudar.
options: Vale doesn't want to help.
It's not that Vale doesn't want to help.
Vale wants me to help.

readAndPick.es: Al parecer, Tomás se vuelve a Canadá.
options: Apparently, Tomás is going back to Canada.
Tomás is sure he is going back to Canada.
Tomás went back to Canada.

readAndPick.es: Por lo visto, Altamira ya compró tres edificios.
options: Altamira will buy three buildings.
I saw Altamira buy three buildings.
Apparently, Altamira has already bought three buildings.

readAndPick.es: No es que tenga miedo, es que no tengo plata.
options: I am afraid because I have no money.
It's not that I'm afraid, it's that I have no money.
I am not afraid and I have money.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No es que ___ de ti.* (*dudo* or *dude*) It's not that I doubt you.
yourTurn.answer: No es que dude de ti.
yourTurn.why: After *no es que* the verb takes the wish form, because you are rejecting the idea: *dude*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Al parecer, el permiso ___ falso.* (*era* or *fuera*) Apparently, the permit was fake.
yourTurn.answer: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.
yourTurn.why: *Al parecer* only passes the news along, so the verb stays plain: *era*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Supposedly, the café closes in December.
yourTurn.answer: Supuestamente, el café cierra en diciembre.
accept: Supuestamente el café cierra en diciembre.
yourTurn.why: *Supuestamente* opens the sentence and the verb stays plain: *cierra*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Apparently, nobody knows where it is.
yourTurn.answer: Por lo visto, nadie sabe dónde está.
accept: Al parecer, nadie sabe dónde está.
Por lo visto nadie sabe dónde está.
Al parecer nadie sabe dónde está.
yourTurn.why: *Por lo visto* and *al parecer* both mean "apparently", so either one works.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It's not that Vale doesn't want to help.
yourTurn.answer: No es que Vale no quiera ayudar.
yourTurn.why: *Quiera* is the wish form of *querer*, and it follows *no es que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn this fact into hearsay with *por lo visto*: *Altamira ya compró tres edificios.*
yourTurn.answer: Por lo visto, Altamira ya compró tres edificios.
accept: Por lo visto Altamira ya compró tres edificios.
Altamira ya compró tres edificios, por lo visto.
yourTurn.why: *Por lo visto* tells the listener you are only passing it on.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It's not that I'm afraid, it's that I have no money.
yourTurn.answer: No es que tenga miedo, es que no tengo plata.
yourTurn.why: *Tenga* is the wish form after *no es que*, while the real reason after *es que* is plain: *no tengo*.

pitfalls.wrong: No es que dudo de ti.
pitfalls.right: No es que dude de ti.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *no es que* the verb takes the wish form, because you are pushing the idea away.

pitfalls.wrong: Al parecer, el permiso fuera falso.
pitfalls.right: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Al parecer* just reports, so the verb stays plain.

pitfalls.wrong: Al parecer que el permiso era falso.
pitfalls.right: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Al parecer* is a short opener with a comma, with no *que* after it.

pitfalls.wrong: Supuestamente, yo vi que Altamira compró el edificio.
pitfalls.right: Yo vi que Altamira compró el edificio.
pitfalls.why: If you saw it yourself you vouch for it, so there is nothing to hedge.

personal: Think of a rumour about your office, your street or your family. Pass it on with *por lo visto* or *al parecer*, then add one thing you are not saying with *no es que*.
